final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor supplied no new admissible evidence and mainly reframed the same record more narrowly. That reframing is directionally more accurate than the earlier overbroad compliance theory, but it still does not satisfy the policy predicate. The admissible evidence shows a 1.2-point miss in a segment named in two pilot commitments, an open legal disclosure question, and a policy requiring disclosure of material limitations for named launch use cases unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. No evidence shows disclosure occurred or that risk acceptance was approved. A caveated statement may be a more faithful description of operational readiness, but it is not enough for compliant_with_caveats here because the caveat is itself the unresolved compliance condition, not a peripheral limitation.
remaining_concerns: No new admissible evidence shows the legal-intake-triage limitation was disclosed to the named pilot commitments before launch.
No approved risk-acceptance record is in evidence for the named launch use case.
Legal review remains open, so the disclosure predicate is unresolved on the admissible record.
The affected segment is named in two law-firm pilot commitments, so product's non-core framing does not defeat materiality under policy.
Aggregate readiness, clean rehearsal, and public governance guidance remain supporting context only and do not satisfy the internal disclosure requirement.
